title: Embolie pulmonaire Syncope-Anemia-Renal Dysfunction (PE-SARD) score
abbreviations: Pulmonary Embolism Syncope Anemia Renal Dysfunction
formula:
Points were assigned to variables to create a point-score model for prediction of early major bleeding:

| Variable | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anemia | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 2.5 | |
| Syncope | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 1.5 | |
| Renal dysfunction | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 1 | |

how_to_use.why:
- Most major bleeds after initiating anticoagulation for PE occur within the first week.
- This score is purpose-built for this very-early risk window, unlike broader bleeding scores.
- It is quick and bedside-friendly, requiring only 3 routinely-available variables.
how_to_use.when:
- À appliquer chez les patients adultes (≥18 ans) chez qui une embolie pulmonaire (EP) est diagnostiquée au service des urgences ou en début d’hospitalisation.
- À utiliser idéalement avant, ou immédiatement après, la première dose d’anticoagulation, afin d’estimer le risque d’hémorragie majeure précoce dans les 7 premiers jours du traitement.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Derived from cohorts that included both hemodynamically stable and unstable patients managed with anticoagulation +/- reperfusion.
- Designed to predict in-hospital major bleeding, defined by ISTH criteria:

 - Fatal bleed.
 - Symptomatic bleed in a critical area or organ (e.g., ICH, intraspinal, intraocular, retroperitoneal, intra-articular, pericardial, intramuscular with compartment syndrome).
 - Hemoglobin drop ≥2 g/dL or requiring transfusion of ≥2 units.
- Not validated for long-term or post-discharge events.
- Renal function was expressed as eGFR calculated with the [CKD-EPI](nabda:calc.ckd-epi-equations-glomerular-filtration-rate-gfr) formula.
- Discrimination in the derivation study was good (C-index ≈ 0.74) and outperformed similar tools (e.g., [VTE-BLEED](nabda:calc.vte-bleed-score) , [RIETE](nabda:calc.riete-score-risk-hemorrhage-pulmonary-embolism-treatment) , BACS); subsequent external validations have yielded mixed results.
- A Swiss validation in older adults (≥65 years of age) did not show accurate prediction for early major bleeding ([Villiger et al., 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37149148/)); more patients were classified into higher-risk strata than the derivation sample, but this did not translate to an observed increased bleeding risk.

next_steps.advice:
- Ce score ne prend pas en compte tous les facteurs de risque hémorragique et doit compléter, et non remplacer, une évaluation clinique approfondie.
- Les résultats de l’évaluation du risque peuvent orienter les décisions concernant la thrombolyse systémique, l’anticoagulation et les stratégies alternatives de reperfusion.
next_steps.management:
- **Low-risk individuals:** Proceed with guideline-concordant anticoagulation +/- reperfusion.
- **Higher-risk individuals:**

 - Address modifiable risk factors, such as concomitant antiplatelet or NSAID use.
 - Consider catheter-based therapy or surgical embolectomy rather than systemic thrombolysis.
 - Consider placement of an inferior vena cava filter, particularly if anticoagulation is contraindicated.
 - Favor anticoagulants with lower bleeding risk (e.g., LMWH or DOACs over unfractionated heparin).
 - Institute closer monitoring.

more_info:
Interpretation:

| PE-SARD Score | Risk of Early Major Bleeding |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Low risk |
| 1-2.5 | Intermediate risk |
| >2.5 | High risk |
